terms.definition: Tissue of dead cells forming hollow tubes strengthened by lignin; it carries water and mineral ions from the roots to the stem and leaves.
terms.examiner: Water moves one way only, upwards.

terms.definition: Tissue of elongated living cells with pores in the end walls; it carries dissolved sugars around the plant in both directions.
terms.examiner: The movement of sugars is called translocation.

terms.definition: The loss of water vapour from the leaves, which draws water up the xylem from the roots.
terms.examiner: It is faster when warm, dry, windy and bright.

terms.definition: The movement of dissolved sugars through the phloem to where they are used or stored.
Tiny pores, mostly on the underside of the leaf, that let carbon dioxide in and water vapour out.
terms.examiner: Guard cells open and close them.

terms.definition: A pair of cells around each stoma that control its size.
terms.examiner: Stomata close in the dark or when the plant is short of water.

terms.definition: The layer of leaf cells packed with chloroplasts where most photosynthesis happens.
terms.examiner: They are near the top surface to absorb most light.

terms.definition: Apparatus that measures the rate of water uptake by a shoot, used to estimate the rate of transpiration.
terms.examiner: Almost all the water taken up is lost by transpiration.
